original_observation_preserved: UX original validator exits0 for healthy and two-backslash input. Those recorded outputs are real; calling the latter a malformed GFM width was wrong.
cause: Reviewer applied ordinary inline backslash parity to GFM table cell scanning before checking the target dialect. Regex unit equivalence did not validate semantic expectation.

sources.scope: GFM table escaping and inline parsing order; ordinary example200 alone does not settle repeated backslashes.
table_cell includes escaped_char OR any nonpipe/nonnewline character; raw backslash alternative permits cell scanner to retain slash-prefixed pipes regardless of parity.
unescape_pipes removes the backslash immediately before a pipe before inline parsing.

finding: Actual GitHub GFM renderer puts rows1/2/3/4 in the same three cells with final tail preserved. Row0 splits and drops the excess tail. Thus original UX negative-lookbehind behavior is correct for this example.
disposition: Do not ship the proposed parity-aware UX regex. Original six retained owner controls remain independently accepted at4aa28e1076b90c626e7339cb898706fc026c42c3. Keep bounded row/header claims; no universal Markdown parser acceptance.
further_scope: Other owners use a deliberately bounded table helper; this correction does not certify their grammar against GFM. If GFM compatibility is required, compare the exact helper contract against rendered controls rather than copying an assumption.
